title: Planner-loaded extension rules (AGENTS.md → planner core)
summary: Move extension/agent-behavior rules from agent-plan AGENTS.md into a planner-loaded ruleset (plan-core + plan_init seeding + surfaced at load) so every project gets them.
description:
Separate planner **extension rules** (behavior that must apply to EVERY project using the agent-plan extension) from **agent-plan development-process rules** (how we build the extension). Today both live in agent-plan's `AGENTS.md`, so only agent-plan gets the extension rules; other projects consuming the extension (MCP, Codex, future harnesses) do not.

CURRENT STATE (packages/agent-plan/AGENTS.md):
- The file mixes two concerns. The header frames it as "regole fondamentali per chiunque lavori su questo progetto" and as "governance indipendente del planner".
- Extension rules currently embedded (must MOVE to planner loading): §1 planner=source-of-truth + update on state change; §2 task lifecycle (task_start/task_complete immediate sync, status=truth); §3 markdown not source-of-truth; §5 plan lives in `.planner/`; §6 discuss plan per phase; §7 P/T global numbering + slug; §8 statusLog + motivation; §10 composite/shortId refs, no UUID, efficient list-search; §12 handoff per-entity + handoff hygiene + update discipline (proactive start, immediate close); the "Avvio del planner" block (web UI never auto-starts, URL only on recap/web-status); the "Regola dettagli (task/phase/feature)" block; the "Comportamento atteso" points 2–5 (read planner entities, update before/after).
- Development-process rules that STAY in AGENTS.md (agent-plan only): §4 core harness-agnostic architecture; §9 stack; §11 requirement sources = AGENTS/PROJECT/ROADMAP.md; §13 Branching & Release (develop/main/next, pnpm release, CI); §14 AGENTS.md modification policy; §15 GSD ban ("in questo progetto"); the Pre-flight Protocol (git/CI/release/lockfile mutations); "Comportamento atteso" point 1 ("leggi AGENTS.md").

GOAL / MECHANISM (agreed with user 2026-08-21):
1. Canonical **ruleset in `plan-core`** — e.g. `packages/plan-core/src/planner-rules.ts` (structured data) holding the extension rules; the planner always has them, zero dependency on AGENTS.md.
2. **`plan_init` seeds** them into `.planner/` (a `rules` field in `project.json` or a dedicated file) so a project can see/override them.
3. **Load flow surfaces** them to the agent — the extension (pi-adapter / MCP) includes the rules in the agent context / recap at `planner load`, so every project receives them.
4. **AGENTS.md shrinks** to only dev-process rules (§4, §9, §11, §13, §14, §15, Pre-flight, "leggi AGENTS.md"), and its header is rewritten to state it governs ONLY the development of the extension.

BEHAVIORS TO PRESERVE: every current behavior described by the moved sections must remain identical after the move — the rules are relocated, not changed in meaning. This aligns with AGENTS.md §3 (markdown is a generated view, not source of truth) and §4 (core is harness-agnostic): the source of the rules becomes `.planner/`/plan-core, not the markdown.

This task is the planner-product counterpart of the task-ordering rule discussion: rules must come FROM the planner at load, portable across all projects.

acceptedDecisions.title: Extension rules relocated to a static plan-core ruleset + .planner/rules.json
acceptedDecisions.decision: Le regole di comportamento del planner vivono come set canonico STATICO in packages/plan-core/src/planner-rules.ts e vengono riepilogate come file .planner/rules.json (senza timestamp) da plan_init. Vengono surface in buildRecap (usato da pi-adapter e plan-mcp al load). AGENTS.md non porta più le regole estensione.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: L'utente ha richiesto che le regole siano statiche (nessun timestamp) per evitare che worktree/branch diversi creino modifiche di data/timestamp che sfociano in conflitti. Tenerle fuori da project.json (ricco di timestamp) e in un file separato privo di timestamp impedisce qualsiasi divergenza.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: init scrive rules.json (statico, {extensionRules:[...]}, nessun timestamp); loadExtensionRules(plannerRoot) lo legge con fallback al set canonico di codice; PlanStore.extensionRules() lo espone; buildRecap aggiunge la sezione '## Planner rules (extension)' nel recap. Schema ProjectSchema invariato (nessun campo in project.json). Verificato: 13 regole, nessun campo timestamp, file identico fra due init, recap contiene la sezione, pnpm check pulito, plan-core test 193/202 (9 pre-esistenti, non correlati).

tasks.title: Relocate extension rules from AGENTS.md into planner-loaded ruleset
tasks.description:
Implement the agreed split: planner **extension/agent-behavior rules** move out of agent-plan's `AGENTS.md` into a **planner-loaded ruleset** (plan-core + plan_init seeding + surfaced at `planner load`), while **agent-plan development-process rules** remain in AGENTS.md.

CODE REFERENCES / TOUCH POINTS:
- Source of rules to move: `/Users/antonio/projects/agent-plan/AGENTS.md` — sections §1, §2, §3, §5, §6, §7, §8, §10, §12, the "Avvio del planner" block, the "Regola dettagli (task/phase/feature)" block, and "Comportamento atteso" points 2–5.
- New canonical ruleset: add `packages/plan-core/src/planner-rules.ts` (or equivalent) exporting the structured extension rules (status=truth, task lifecycle, naming, refs/shortId, handoff hygiene, web-not-auto-start, etc.).
- Seeding: extend `plan_init` / the project schema so the rules are written into `.planner/` (e.g. a `rules` field in `project.json` or a dedicated `.planner/rules` file), defaulting from the plan-core canonical set.
- Surfacing: the extension load flow (pi-adapter `src/index.ts` and/or `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`) must include the loaded rules in the agent context / recap at `planner load`, so any project receives them without AGENTS.md.
- Trimming: remove the moved sections from `AGENTS.md`, keep only §4, §9, §11, §13, §14, §15, Pre-flight, and "Comportamento atteso" point 1; rewrite the header to state AGENTS.md governs ONLY the development of the extension.

CONCRETE STEPS:
1. Enumerate the exact extension-rule text to relocate (use the phase description categorization as the source of truth).
2. Define the canonical ruleset in plan-core as structured, loadable data (single source of truth for these rules).
3. Have `plan_init` seed the rules into `.planner/` so projects can view/override; planner always falls back to the embedded canonical set.
4. Wire the extension load to read + surface the rules to the agent (context/recap).
5. Strip the moved sections from AGENTS.md and rewrite its header as dev-process-only.
6. Verify in a throwaway project (mkdtemp, NOT a real project dir) that `plan_init` + `planner load` yields the rules WITHOUT any AGENTS.md present.
7. `pnpm check` + existing plan-core/extension tests green.

EDGE CASES:
- A project may have an older `.planner/` without the `rules` field → planner must use the embedded canonical defaults (no crash, no AGENTS.md dependency).
- Override semantics: project `.planner/` rules should be allowed to extend/override the canonical set; define that contract.
- Do NOT change the *meaning* of any rule during relocation — only its source location.

WHY: AGENTS.md is agent-plan-specific governance. The extension rules must be portable to every project that uses the extension (MCP, Codex, future harnesses), loaded by the planner at startup — consistent with AGENTS.md §3 (markdown is a generated view, not source of truth) and §4 (core harness-agnostic).

Implementata la localizzazione delle regole estensione. Nuovo packages/plan-core/src/planner-rules.ts con PLANNER_EXTENSION_RULES (13 regole statiche) + loadExtensionRules(plannerRoot) (legge .planner/rules.json con fallback al set canonico di codice). plan-store.ts: init() ora scrive .planner/rules.json STATICO ({extensionRules:[...]}, zero timestamp) e aggiunge metodo extensionRules(). recap.ts: buildRecap espone la sezione "## Planner rules (extension)". index.ts: export. AGENTS.md: riscritto mantenendo solo le regole di sviluppo (§4,§9,§11,§13,§14,§15,Pre-flight,Discuss), con header che rimanda a planner-rules.ts. Progettualmente le regole NON sono in project.json (evito divergenza timestamp). Verificato: pnpm --filter @agent-plan/core check pulito; recap.test.mjs 12/12; plan-core suite 193/202 (gli stessi 9 pre-esistenti del branch t253); test mkdtemp: rules.json con solo chiave extensionRules (nessun timestamp), identico fra due init, recap contiene la sezione regole. Per vedere le regole nel recap live di pi-adapter occorre ricostruire pi-adapter (pnpm build:pi-adapter) poiché l'adattatore importa plan-core a runtime.
